newsitem.title: USA: Daschle hopeful on balanced U.S. budget agreement.
newsitem.headline: Daschle hopeful on balanced U.S. budget agreement.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota said he was optimistic that agreement could be reached with majority Republicans on a plan to balance the federal budget by the year 2002.

Daschle told reporters the deficit as a percentage of gross domestic product was at its lowest since 1974. "I don't think there's any question that Democrats are determined as we've ever been to finish the job. So we feel we've made extremely remarkable progress in the last several years. We want to finish the job and there's no reason we can't finish the job before the year 2002, on or before."

"I've had many opportunities to talk with (Senate Majority Leader Trent) Lott over the last several weeks. And I feel very good about the goodwill and the optimism and the hope that he and I can express as we begin our effort today," Daschle said.
He said other legislation Democrats wanted to act on included campaign finance reform, education and health care.
Republicans have a 55-45 Senate majority, two more seats than they had in the last session of Congress, and many of the new senators are considered more conservative than the members they replaced.
Daschle said the chances for a tax cut this year depended on the overall budget agreement and on revenue offsets.

"I think the president has said he'll work with Republicans in finding ways with which to provide some tax relief. But it ought to be targeted, it ought to be dedicated in large measure to those who need it the most and it has to be paid for."
Daschle said he did not think a national sales tax would be approved anytime in the foreseeable future.
